hook: The queen who reigned for 70 years, from Churchill to the age of the internet.

pages.x: Elizabeth was born in London in 1926, and was not expected to be queen. In 1936 her uncle, King Edward VIII, gave up the throne to marry an American divorcée, and her father became king. She was ten. Her family called her Lilibet.

In the Second World War she joined the army's women's service at 18, and trained as a mechanic and lorry driver. On the night the war in Europe ended, she and her sister slipped out to join the cheering crowds.
On her 21st birthday, in 1947, speaking on the radio from Cape Town, she promised to give her whole life, whether long or short, to serving the peoples of the Commonwealth.

In February 1952, on a tour of Kenya, she spent a night at a hotel built in a fig tree, watching wild animals at a waterhole. That night her father died. It was said she climbed the tree a princess and came down a queen.
She was crowned in Westminster Abbey in June 1953. It was the first coronation shown on television, and millions of people bought their first set to watch it.
During her reign most of the British Empire became independent. She became head of the Commonwealth, a club of 56 countries, and over her life she was queen of 32 different nations.
She owned more than 30 corgis over her life. For the opening of the London Olympics in 2012, she starred in a film with James Bond, in which she seemed to parachute into the stadium.
She reigned for 70 years, longer than any other British monarch, and worked with 15 prime ministers, the first of them Winston Churchill. She died at Balmoral in 2022, aged 96.
Elizabeth II was a symbol of steadiness through seven decades of change, from the end of empire to the age of the internet.
